newsitem.title: USA: Safety group rates Camry 'best' in crash test.
newsitem.headline: Safety group rates Camry 'best' in crash test.

text.p: Crash results for the new Toyota Motor Corp. Camry earned a "best pick" evaluation Monday from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
In other tests of midsize, four-door cars, the industry-backed group rated the General Motors Corp. Pontiac Grand Prix "acceptable" and the Hyundai Motor Co. Ltd. Sonata "poor."
"Best picks" among midsize four-door cars announced earlier were the Ford Motor Co. Taurus/Mercury Sable, the GMC Chevrolet Lumina and the Volvo 850.

The group said the chief component of the rating is a 40 miles-per-hour frontal crash to show how well the vehicle structure manages the crash and the risk of injury measured with a dummy representing an average-size male driver.

"The new Camry, Taurus, Lumina and Volvo demonstrate the crash-worthiness automakers can, and should, achieve with all of their midsize models," said institute President Brian O'Neill. "Unfortunately, we still have too many poor performers like the Sonata."
The institute said the Sonata joins six other midsize four-door cars with poor evaluations.

They are the Nissan Motor Co. Ltd. Maxima, the Chrysler Corp. Chrysler Cirrus/Dodge Stratus/Plymouth Breeze, the Mitsubishi Motors Corp. Galant, GMC's Chevrolet Cavalier/Pontiac Sunfire, the Volkswagen AG Passat, and Ford's Ford Contour/Mercury Mystique.
